title: OpenClaw hosting: managed offers versus madani cloud
h1: openclaw hosting or a different cloud bot app?
description: Compare Hostinger and Elestio managed OpenClaw with madani cloud: promotional rates, renewal costs, included care and the decisions that remain yours.
answer: **get your weekends back without giving up openclaw.** managed hosting keeps the assistant you chose and hands server care to someone else. madani cloud runs a different product: madani bots, chats, memory and routines. choose the assistant first, then compare renewal rates and ai charges. the opening rate is only part of what you'll pay.[^1][^2][^3][^4]

review.by: lead agent: read against seo/facts, automated gate, independent fact-check pass

og_line: the host is only part of the bill.

them: **keep openclaw's channels and skills.** let a host handle server care.
**pay for upkeep rather than a product move.** you already want the open-source project.
madani: **keep named madani bots.** each has its own chats on your dedicated hosted computer.
**move existing madani work off your laptop.** bring chats, memory and routines to madani cloud.

compare.intro: **put the renewal beside the offer before you compare hosts.** prices are as of 12 november 2026; hostinger's promotion varies by region. these services run different products, so choose the assistant as well as the machine.

method:
**compare the bill and the upkeep each host says it handles.** we sell madani cloud. hostinger and elestio offers were checked on 12 november 2026.

maintenance descriptions come from the hosts. we didn't test uptime, run matching jobs or benchmark machines. the prices show what you pay for hosting; task costs also depend on ai usage.

sections.h: read the term beside the rate
sections.md:
**$4.99 monthly asks for $119.76 up front.** hostinger's promotion covers a 24-month term and renews at $11.99 monthly. those terms are from 12 november 2026; region and date can change them.[^1]

elestio starts at $16 monthly, including compute, storage, bandwidth, updates and backups.[^2]

madani cloud plus costs $20 monthly or $200 yearly. pro costs $50 monthly or $500 yearly and includes one person's work license.[^4] ai usage costs extra.[^5] use the [cost tool](/tools/always-on-cost) with both bills in mind.

sections.h: managed doesn't choose what the agent may touch
sections.md:
**pay the host to patch the server; choose the agent's reach yourself.** hostinger and elestio describe handling security and backups.[^1][^2] openclaw's skills and plugins still need your judgement.[^6] use the [safety guide](/guides/is-openclaw-safe) before adding them.

in madani, start a new bot with read only access.[^7] for app edits later, put 'ask me before changing anything' into the routine.[^7]

sections.h: choose the assistant before the server
sections.md:
**if openclaw fits, hosting may be all you need.** its [desktop installers](/alternatives/openclaw-no-setup) also reduce setup work.[^8]

madani cloud moves existing madani chats, memory and routines.[^4] moving from openclaw means rebuilding the jobs, instructions and schedules in madani; there's no importer.

look at the finished job, even when someone else handles the machine. server backups cover the server; don't count on them to restore every connected service.

faq.q: is there an official hosted openclaw?
faq.a: **the project says it has no hosted tier.** hostinger and elestio sell third-party offers. look at who handles support and who gets your payment.[^6][^1][^2]
**the mit software is free; hosting costs money.** these managed offers charge for the machine and care. ai usage has its own arrangement.[^6][^3]

faq.q: do i need to buy a mac mini to keep an agent running?
faq.a: **no, these routes use hosted servers.** madani cloud keeps bots available with your computer off too. a mac mini has purchase and power costs outside this comparison.[^1][^2][^4]
